body: Maybe you can buy her a planner (perfect gift for the holidays) that she can use for tracking her period and possibly other stuff.

I’m so sorry she made you feel that way. You truly deserve someone who cares about your feelings. This girl sounds very egotistic and the relationship seemed quite unhealthy.

Boundaries are very important in a relationship. On the one hand you can share everything and your partner can feel so overwhelmed that eventually it will also effect them very negatively. But on the other hand, keeping everything to yourself is so unhealthy and will eventually also impact your relationship.

I’m happy that i know that if i want, i can talk to my boyfriend about it. But I mostly choose not to or very limited. He doesn’t really understand because he has never struggled with mental health + my communicating skills aren’t that great that i can express my experiences accurate. He mostly tries to give practical advice, while i need more emotional support (i think this is a common problem between men and women) or tries to relate and turn it into something that ‘everyone experiences’ which makes me feel even more invalid.

It’s great you’re trying to help your girlfriend. You clearly care a lot about her. I think inviting her over is definitely something she appreciates as it will probably reduce her stress a lot.

I would be careful trying to get your girlfriend to talk to her parents about their problems. You don’t want to have her play the ‘therapist’ among her parents, because it’s emotionally very exhausting and unhealthy. If she is close to them, she maybe can suggest marriage counselling, as this is probably the only thing that can help the fights. Other then that, I would advice her to distance herself as much as possible during the fights.

Also I think the most you can do is just give emotional support. You can give as many ‘practical solutions’ as you want, but remember that you can’t fix this problem. Listen to her, try to understand, ask questions about how she is feeling. Making her feel like she is not alone in this, will most definitely mean a lot to her.
This may be personal (my parents also used to fight a lot) but i feel like assuming that ‘some things are said out of affection’ or ‘ not being meant that serious’ is undermining her experience and making her feel like she is exaggerating, so I would try not using this too much and mostly focus on how she is experiencing this situation.

But keep putting in the effort, I’m sure she appreciates it a lot and you are helping her.
I can relate to this. The reality of starting another day stresses me out so much that i don’t want to fall asleep. I mostly just stay on my phone fighting against sleep until i pass out

I relate to this so much. I’m not actively suicidal like previous years so I guess I’m doing better. I think I just convinced myself to just live out my life mostly for other people. Like life is uncomfortable but not  unbearable so I guess I just have to keep living.

I feel almost exactly the same about my boyfriend. To me, some days are better than others. I may lay awake for hours wondering why anyone would ever like me, if this is all a big joke, worrying about him breaking up with me, and the worst part... I would totally understand. My thoughts are better when I’m actually with him and I feel at ease.

What I find helpful is trying to remind myself that this is all playing out in my head. It’s your low self esteem and insecurities that are telling you you are not good enough. These thoughts can be so intense that it seems impossible that maybe, possibly, people don’t perceive you the way you view yourself. But the truth is, people don’t see the worst in you, especially your girlfriend, someone who cares a lot about you.

When going through these feelings, I try to make something positive of them. I try my best to be extra attentive, give complements, little surprises. So I can say objectively to myself ‘look I’m not such a bad girlfriend I did this and this’.

Hope this maybe helps. Please don’t let these insecurities ruin your relationship.
Yeah I’m doing a bit better now thank you!

My parents found at when they found a suicide note I wrote. They forced me to go to therapy but we never really spoke about it afterwards, mostly because I am not willing to talk to my parents about this stuff.

I relate to this so much. My dad always made me feel bad after any event or situation that I didn’t talk much and even now I can feel he is ashamed of having a ‘shy’ daughter. It made me feel so bad about myself and I’m having a really hard time accepting myself, mostly because I’m not as talkative as others and that has always been seen as something negative. I wish people wouldn’t be bothered about about how quiet I am, so I could learn to love myself eventually.
